data: Dark, carbon-rich (C-type) near-Earth asteroid shaped like a spinning top, about 900 m across. JAXA's Hayabusa2 arrived in June 2018, dropped rovers on the surface, fired a copper impactor to make an artificial crater and touched down twice in 2019. Its capsule brought 5.4 g of Ryugu back to Earth in December 2020 — water-bearing material little changed since the solar system formed.
Hayabusa2 — JAXA, 2018–2019 rendezvous, two touchdowns and an artificial crater; 2020 sample return
Ryugu is a near-Earth Apollo asteroid — semi-major axis 1.19 AU, close enough to Earth's orbit for Hayabusa2 to reach it, stay 17 months and bring samples home in 2020.
Half the longest diameter of the orbit ellipse — and the single number that sets the orbital period.
